comment: Results of the oracles that need an external tool and a cloned corpus, so they cannot run in `pnpm test`. Refreshed by `CODEINDEX_ORACLE=1 vitest run tests/oracles-external-diff.test.ts` and by the weekly e2e workflow. Committed WITH provenance because the site publishes these numbers: a figure with no tool version, corpus or date is not a measurement, it is a claim. Figures move slightly with the external tool's version — the weekly CI run measured ctags recall on ripgrep at 0.9861 against the 0.9799 recorded here, on a different ctags build.

ctags.note: The lower TypeScript figures are largely ctags SURPLUS rather than gaps of ours: it tags function-body locals and quoted config keys, which a declaration index deliberately omits — on code-du-travail we report 1904 declarations ctags does not. The figures rose across every repository after the differential named three real clusters (Go package clauses, Python PEP 484 re-exports, Rust in-function const/static) and they were fixed; gin moved 0.9127 → 0.9858.

typescriptCompiler.corpus: t3-oss/create-t3-turbo, the 53 files all three tools indexed
typescriptCompiler.note: Recall against an index built by the real TypeScript compiler — authoritative on TypeScript where both ctags and this engine are syntactic. Scoped to NAMED declarations: the indexer also emits a synthetic descriptor per object-literal key, which is not a declaration and is excluded.

calibration.note: How far ctags can be trusted as an oracle on the 39 languages the compiler-based one cannot check. All 5 misses are one construct: string-literal declaration names (module augmentations, quoted interface keys).
